神经退行性疾病.title: Intrastriatal injection of amplified Lewy body dementia (LBD) fibrils in mice results in accumulation of fibrils with LBD structure and neurodegeneration
神经退行性疾病.abstract: The defining neuropathologic feature of Lewy body dementia (LBD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) is alpha-synuclein (Asyn) fibril accumulation in Lewy bodies (LBs) and Lewy neurites (LNs). Recently, we developed a method to amplify Asyn fibrils derived from human post-mortem LBD brain tissue and determined that the structure of amplified Asyn fibrils is highly similar to the structure of fibrils directly isolated from LBD brain tissue. We examined whether injection of these fibrils into humanized Asyn mice recapitulates pathologic Asyn fibril accumulation with human LBD Asyn fibril structure. We utilized mice containing a null allele in the mouse Snca gene and a human SNCA transgene. Intrastriatal injection of amplified Asyn fibrils derived from 3 different LBD autopsy cases resulted in cytoplasmic and neuritic phospho-Asyn accumulation in the striatum, cortex, and amygdala bilaterally at 3mpi. Fibril injections produced a reduction in the number of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, with LB-like inclusions in surviving neurons, and produced impaired sensorimotor function as measured on the accelerating rotarod test. Fibril accumulation increased 3.6-fold between 1 and 3 months post-injection (mpi) and was relatively stable between 3 and 5 mpi. We amplified fibrils from mouse brain tissue 5 mpi and collected single-particle cryo-EM data. High resolution 3D structural information could not be obtained because of the lack of helical twist, but comparison of the cryo-EM 2D class averages with those derived from amplified fibrils prepared from human LBD tissue revealed multiple matching classes, indicating that the Lewy fold is maintained in the fibrils that accumulate in mouse brain tissue. Our findings demonstrate an approach to model the accumulation of Asyn fibrils with LBD structure in mice, providing a platform for investigating disease mechanisms, imaging biomarkers, and therapeutics targeting Asyn in PD/LBD.

神经退行性疾病.title: Integration of Neuroimaging and Histopathology in a Squirrel Monkey Model of Spontaneous Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy and Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is a prevalent cerebrovascular pathology in AD and contributes to amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), a major complication of current anti-amyloid immunotherapy. Despite its growing clinical importance, critical gaps remain in the development of reliable biomarkers for antemortem diagnosis of CAA. Squirrel monkeys (SQMs) are a valuable non-human primate model with translational relevance due to their universal propensity to develop abundant CAA and spontaneous ARIA in geriatric animals. The present study employed R2*, the apparent transverse relaxation rate, which is sensitive to susceptibility-related tissue properties, including iron content and blood oxygenation levels, to monitor age-related brain pathology in SQMs with varying CAA severity. Young, early geriatric, and late geriatric SQMs underwent 7T MRI using a dual-purpose T2*-w 3D multi-gradient-echo sequence for high-resolution anatomy and quantitative R2* mapping, alongside T2-w/FLAIR imaging. Whole-brain and gray matter R2* increased with age. In contrast, white matter R2* showed an initial increase followed by a late-life reversal, likely reflecting age-related changes in myelin integrity, tissue microstructure, and tissue water content. MRI-histopathology correlation linked T2*-w MRI hypointensities to CAA-positive iron-laden vessels associated with perivascular inflammation and, in some cases, hemosiderin deposits. Here we confirmed the occurrence of ARIA-H and ARIA-E events in geriatric animals. SQMs provided a valuable opportunity to examine the underlying pathology of spontaneous ARIA-E, revealing distinctive tissue signatures associated with its manifestation. ARIA-E hyperintensities were characterized by reactive gliosis and BBB disruption, whereas more advanced lesions exhibited perivascular lymphocytic infiltration and evidence of myelin and axonal injury. The current study presents compelling evidence linking R2* alterations with CAA severity and ARIA

神经退行性疾病.title: Trigeminal Nerve Stimulation Attenuates Traumatic Brain Injury-Induced Neuronal Damage via CGRP-PINK1 Mitophagy Axis
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Secondary damage after traumatic brain injury (TBI) is driven by progressive mitochondrial failure, yet clinically viable strategies to directly safeguard mitochondrial networks remain a major therapeutic gap. Here, we show that non-invasive trigeminal nerve stimulation (TNS), which engages the brain's endogenous oxygen-conserving diving reflex, preserves neuronal survival by directly regulating the mitochondrial PINK1/Parkin quality-control pathway. We demonstrate that TBI induces the pathological aggregation of the outer mitochondrial membrane receptor TOM20, in a CGRP-dependent manner, which affects binding of the damage-sensor PINK1 and renders downstream Parkin-mediated rescue ineffective. TNS-induced neuronal CGRP release prevents this TOM20 aggregation, restoring proper PINK1 function and downstream Parkin activation. This preservation of mitochondrial architecture reinforces the outer membrane's barrier function, limiting pro-apoptotic cytochrome c leakage and supporting NRF2 antioxidant defenses, ultimately reducing progressive infarct expansion and recovering sensorimotor functions. The significance of this work lies in bridging physical neuromodulation directly to the preservation of organelle-level architecture. By demonstrating that stimulation of trigeminal afferents to recruit an oxygen-conserving reflex can stabilize outer membrane signaling architecture and preserve mitochondrial survival machinery, this study outlines a non-pharmacological strategy to protect mitochondrial function and inhibit acute post-traumatic neurodegeneration.

神经退行性疾病.title: ASC specks and α-synuclein amplify microglial NLRP3 inflammasome activation and co-localize with Lewy body pathology
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of several chronic neurodegenerative disorders, including Parkinson's disease (PD) and other synucleinopathies, and is closely associated with microglial activation. The inflammasome adaptor protein apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase activation and recruitment domain (ASC) undergoes oligomerization upon inflammasome activation, resulting in the formation of ASC specks. These structures are recognized by microglia as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), thereby promoting inflammatory signaling. Recent studies have demonstrated that extracellular ASC specks associate with amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}), and that uptake of ASC-A{beta} composites by microglia amplifies pro-inflammatory responses. Although ASC specks have also been shown to potentiate -synuclein (Syn) preformed fibril-induced pathology, their interaction with monomeric Syn and their effects on inflammasome activation remain poorly understood. Here, we co-stimulated murine SIM-A9 microglia with ASC-Syn assemblies and evaluated their effects on NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Electron microscopy revealed a close association between ASC fibrils and Syn monomers. Exposure of microglia to ASC-Syn enhanced NLRP3 inflammasome activation, as evidenced by increased ASC speck formation, caspase-1 activation, and secretion of IL-1{beta} and IL-18, when compared to ASC or Syn alone. In addition, immunohistochemical analyses of post mortem brain tissue from patients with dementia with Lewy bodies demonstrated ASC expression in regions exhibiting Syn pathology and showed ASC co-localization with Syn within Lewy bodies. Collectively, these findings identify ASC-Syn assemblies as potent amplifiers of NLRP3 inflammasome signaling and suggest a mechanism through which they may contribute to sustained neuroinflammation in synucleinopathies.

神经退行性疾病.title: Astrocyte-Specific dsRNA-ADAR1 Signalling Links Innate Immunity to Complement Activation in Parkinson Disease
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Background: Dysregulated innate immune activation is a key feature of Parkinson disease (PD), but the upstream triggers and cell-type-specific mechanisms remain unclear. Double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) has emerged as a potential driver of innate immune responses. Adenosine deaminase acting on RNA 1 (ADAR1), particularly its interferon-inducible p150 isoform, edits dsRNA to limit aberrant immune activation. Whether this dsRNA-ADAR1 axis contributes to neuroinflammation in PD in a cell-type-specific manner is unknown. Methods: We performed immunofluorescence on post-mortem cingulate cortex tissue from PD cases and controls to localise dsRNA, ADAR1 p150 and pathological alpha-synuclein protein. We integrated these findings with single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from three independent human brain datasets. An eight-module gene scoring framework was applied to assess dsRNA processing, sensing, and downstream innate immune pathways in neurons and astrocytes. Results: In PD cortex, the proportion of dsRNA-positive astrocytes was higher than in controls, whereas neuronal dsRNA positivity did not differ between groups. ADAR1 p150 positivity increased in both astrocytes and neurons, and the proportion of ADAR1 p150 positive astrocytes correlated with astrocytic -synuclein burden. Transcriptomic analyses showed that neurons were enriched for dsRNA editing and processing machinery, whereas astrocytes exhibited higher expression of dsRNA sensing pathways, innate immune responses, and transposable element control. While overall pathway activity did not differ between PD and controls after covariate adjustment, network analyses revealed cell-type-specific coupling patterns. Notably, complement gene expression showed a strong and selective association with dsRNA-related pathways in astrocytes, whereas interferon and NF-{kappa}B signalling were shared across cell types. 神经退行性疾病.title: Single Cell Proteomics reveals partial uncoupling of the Glycerol-3-Phosphate shuttle to compensate for Electron Transport Chain dysfunction in Alexander Disease GFAP mutations
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare genetic leukodystrophy caused by dominant mutations in the gene coding for the astrocytic intermediate filament protein Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP). Understanding disease mechanisms is complicated by the fact that mutant GFAP promotes further GFAP accumulation, making it difficult to distinguish mutation-specific effects from those caused by elevated GFAP levels. Here, we performed mass spectrometry-based single cell proteomics to investigate proteomic alterations associated with increasing levels of wildtype GFAP and a common AxD-causing mutant GFAP R239C. By analyzing individual cells spanning a broad range of GFAP expression levels, we separated dosage-dependent effects from mutation-specific responses. Cells expressing high levels of wildtype GFAP increasingly resembled R239C-expressing cells at the proteomic level, supporting a role for GFAP accumulation in disease pathogenesis. In contrast, mutant GFAP specifically correlated with increased mitochondrial antioxidant enzymes and remodeling of the proteasome tailored toward ATP- and ubiquitin-independent degradation of oxidized proteins. Integration with proteomics data from patient-derived cortical organoids revealed increased abundance of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins and respiratory chain assembly factors without corresponding changes in mitochondrially encoded proteins, suggesting impaired electron transport chain (ETC) assembly. Consistent with this, AxD cells displayed reduced oxygen consumption, increased glycolytic activity, enhanced utilization of the cytosolic part of the glycerol-3-phosphate (G3P) shuttle, and accumulation of triacylglycerides and lipid droplets. We propose that ETC dysfunction promotes partial uncoupling of the G3P shuttle, allowing sustained regeneration of cytosolic NAD to support glycolysis while diverting G3P toward lipid synthesis and storage. 神经退行性疾病.title: 5-HT1A Antagonist WAY-100635 Prevents Chronic Neurodegeneration and Immune Activation After TBI
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) initiates secondary neurodegeneration that compromises interconnected neural circuits and contributes to persistent visual and neurobehavioral impairment. Pharmacological strategies that preserve vulnerable neurons and synapses while limiting chronic neuroinflammation remain an unmet therapeutic need. We previously identified the serotonin 1A receptor (5-HT1A) antagonist WAY-100635 through screening human stem cell-derived retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and demonstrated that it promotes neuroprotection through cyclic adenosine monophosphate-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis. Here, we investigated whether post-injury treatment extends this neuroprotective efficacy to cerebral and visual circuitry following TBI. Male C57BL/6J mice aged 2-3 months underwent unilateral controlled cortical impact (CCI) involving the left visual cortex. Mice were randomly assigned to sham, untreated injury or treated injury groups, with 3-10 sham controls and 5-8 mice per injury group across experiments. WAY-100635 was administered intraperitoneally at 5 mg/kg daily, beginning 1 hour after injury and continuing for 6 weeks. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed using motor and psychological-health-relevant risk-taking/behavioral disinhibition by elevated-plus-maze assessment, visual electrophysiology, optokinetic responses, diffusion magnetic resonance imaging, and retinal and cortical histopathology. Unilateral cortical injury produced bilateral RGC dysfunction and loss, with greater degeneration in the eye contralateral to the injured hemisphere, consistent with predominantly crossed murine visual projections. WAY-100635 significantly preserved RGC survival and function, improved visual acuity and contrast sensitivity, and preserved visually evoked cortical responses to contralateral eye stimulation. 神经退行性疾病.title: A rapid, genetically-tractable human iPSC-derived model for studying tissue-resident macrophage biology in Alzheimer's and other diseases
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Large-scale genetic and preclinical studies strongly implicate myeloid cells, particularly brain-resident macrophages, in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Efferocytic clearance of apoptotic cells and other cholesterol-rich cellular debris is a core macrophage function and represents an active area of AD research. However, human tissue-resident macrophages remain difficult to model in vitro as they acquire their transcriptional and functional identities in response to signals from their host tissue microenvironment. Many existing differentiation protocols mimic human brain macrophage developmental trajectories, but these protocols rely either on multi-step cytokine cocktails and lengthy differentiation or transduction of multiple transcription factors, both of which introduce variability and complicate genetic manipulation. To address these limitations, we developed a simplified protocol that generates high-purity (>90% CD45+CD11b+) human iPSC-derived macrophage-like cells (iMacs) from cryopreservable erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMP)-like intermediates in 19 days, including a final 7-day maturation step driven by macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) alone. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that iMacs show enrichment for phagocytic and lysosomal programs, processes integral to efferocytosis. At both the transcriptional and protein level, iMacs have higher expression of scavenger receptors such as CD36, CD163 and MRC1, and of AD risk genes such as TREM2. Functionally, iMacs show enhanced phagocytic uptake of diverse substrates relative to iPSC-derived microglia, including carboxylated latex beads, zymosan, amyloid-{beta} 1-42, and amyloid-{beta} 1-40, and exhibit expanded lysosomal mass.
